## Design

### 2026-10-26: Date: October 26, 2026

**2h**

Date: October 26, 2026

In this session, I came up with an idea for a cabinet lighting system that includes multicolor lights and basic white light. I worked on the schematic layout and input all the necessary parts like the Xiao RP2040, resistors, RKGB LEDs, basic LEDS, a push button, and a potentiometer.  One thing that confused me was the different representation of the RGB labels, where some were labeled RBG or RGBK, which I recognized were used for different purposes, so I looked at the guide for a suggested option and went with the RKGB LEDS.  I also referred to the guide for the resistor values that work for my microcontroller. This concludes the part layout session and in the next session, I will be assigning the footprints and starting the actual PCB design.

### 2026-11-01: Date: November 1, 2026

**4h**

Date: November 1, 2026

In this session, I worked on assigning the footprints to all the components and designed the PCB layout. One thing that confused me for a bit was the parts when I assigned the footprints because I decided to go with my own project idea and I ended up not knowing what the parts were, so I had to refer back to the guide a couple of times for some help. Some of my parts were used from the guide and I mostly picked out the cheapest parts since the high price range wasn't my motive for this project. When I designed the PCB layout, I went with a layout that had minimal wire crossings to make the appearance cleaner. While doing the DRC check, a lot of errors showed up, which I had to take into consideration and find out what went wrong. It turns out that it was a size error with the pads, so I decided to edit the size so that the error would go away and would still allow the part to fit during assembly. After the layout was complete, I moved to the coding part in Arduino. I started with a basic code that defines all the pins and outputs; the rest of the code will be done later when the parts are assembled and I can test its functionality then. The final steps are to manufacture the project and produce the Gerber and Drill files.
